securityBasis.reviewInterpretation: Redis 8.2.8 includes security fixes for crafted RESTORE payloads that the release notes describe as potentially leading to use-after-free, out-of-bounds writes, and remote code execution. The repository policy prevents a silent regression to the previously pinned 8.2.1 or another version below 8.2.8.

reviewedContainerInput.interpretation: The manifest-list identity and source policy were verified, but Docker and Podman were unavailable, so the pinned Alpine image itself was not pulled or executed.

integrationVerification.command: REDIS_URL=<authenticated-loopback-url> pnpm exec vitest run --project integration apps/worker/src/queue.integration.test.ts apps/api/src/rate-limit.integration.test.ts apps/web/src/session-revocation.integration.test.ts

durableQueue: three separate Redis connections coordinate the producer, worker, and queue event stream
one tenant-bound job is processed once and its stable queue identity deduplicates a duplicate add
an invalid capability fails unrecoverably after one attempt without spending a five-attempt retry budget
distributedRateLimit: two separate Redis clients and Fastify instances share one randomized namespace
121 concurrent requests produce exactly 120 successful responses and one 429
exactly one environment-scoped 64-hex HMAC key exists
the key contains no raw loopback address and has a positive TTL
distributedSessionRevocation: two separate Redis-backed stores share one randomized namespace
a logout recorded through one store is enforced through the other
a different session ID for the same subject remains valid
the same JWT ID is classified as replayed across stores
exactly one replay and one session key use 64-hex HMAC indexes
keys contain no raw subject, session ID, or JWT ID and have positive TTLs

limitations: The official source archive was compiled and executed on the host; the pinned Alpine OCI image and Compose network were not executed because Docker and Podman were unavailable.
The server used authenticated loopback TCP without TLS; no production Redis transport, ACL, network policy, sentinel, cluster, or managed-service configuration was exercised.
Two clients and application instances ran in one host process topology, not on separately scheduled machines or containers.
Nginx, ingress, realistic load, Redis startup/runtime failure and recovery, coordinated HMAC/session-secret rotation, and alert delivery remain unexercised.
No authorized Keycloak back-channel delivery, old-cookie denial through two actual Next.js replicas, later-login recovery, or provider clock boundary was exercised.
No production, staging, multi-host, container-runtime, provider, or customer-data result is claimed.
